text_en: exists in ancient copies and exists in present copies. Taking what exists in the present and collating what exists in the ancient, then the ancient may be acceptable, while the present may not yet be. But if one is to take from them, should one take the ancient and call it right? Or take the present and call it right? Or rather take both present and ancient together as right? Alas, what to take and what to discard? Better to collate present and ancient and take what is acceptable. In general, texts circulating in the world under the title Recorded Sayings of the Great Master are mostly spurious compilations. For example, in making sermons to the assembly, they may take something like the verse on the Four Prohibitions and add explanatory words, presenting it as a sermon; from this, one can know the extent of spurious fabrication. As for the recorded sayings of Dong and Cao in China, they were compiled by Guo Limei. These too are present copies, and not yet truly ancient. Even so, though not a perfect jade disk, their luster is not of the sort of worthless Yanshi stones either. Therefore I, unworthy as I am, extracted Master Heyu's teachings from the Record of the Five Houses, taking what should be taken and discarding what should be discarded, and at times using old compilations to fill in what was lacking. Thus the recorded sayings were completed. Ah, when the ancients left teachings for later ages, those who bore their intent acted before us. Their signs and teachings were handed down. We who dwell in later times and bear their intent, how can we stand before them? I, unworthy as I am, therefore wish to gather the ancients' pivotal sayings and correct the true and false of old and new, to spread their teaching more widely and diligently. I venture to ask those in later ages who bear their intent: act for it, enter into it, embody it. If they do so, it may be said that I and the patriarchs ride the same turtle, drifting and swimming together in the deep pond. Would that not be delightful?

text_en: Originally there is not a single thing. The biased rank is precisely the realm of form, where the myriad appearances have shape. The biased within the upright is turning away from principle and going toward phenomena. The upright within the biased is leaving phenomena and entering principle. Combined bearing is darkly responding to all conditions, not falling into any forms of being, neither defiled nor pure, neither upright nor biased. Therefore it is called the empty mysterious great way, the unattached true school. The former worthies from above esteemed this one rank as the most wondrous and most profound. One should examine and distinguish it carefully. The ruler is the upright rank; the minister is the biased rank. Minister facing the ruler is the upright within the biased. Ruler regarding the minister is the biased within the upright. The way of ruler and minister in accord is speech of combined bearing. The monk asked, What is the ruler? The master said, Wondrous virtue honors the world-sphere, lofty brightness illumines the great void. He asked, What is the minister? The master said, Numinous function broadens the sage's way; true wisdom benefits all beings. He asked, What is minister facing ruler? The master said, Not falling into the various divergent destinies, concentrating feeling and gazing on the sage's countenance. He asked, What is ruler regarding minister? The master said, Though the wondrous countenance does not move, its light illumines and originally has no bias. He asked, What is the way of ruler and minister in accord? The master said, Blended together, there is no inside or outside; harmoniously fused, above and below are level. The master also said, In speaking of ruler and minister, biased and upright, one does not wish to violate the center. Therefore the minister addresses the ruler and does not dare call him directly by name. So it is. This is the essential point of my Dharma lineage. Then he composed a verse, saying, Students must first know their own school. Do not mix the true limit with blank emptiness. If the wondrous bright body is exhausted, know that contact wounds it. The power lies in meeting conditions without borrowing the middle. When speaking, let it be such that fire cannot burn it; in hidden practice one must be one with the ancients. No body yet affairs present transcends the branching roads; no affairs and no body falls into beginning and end. text_en: come closer. Shui came closer. The master said, Three cups of wine at the Bai family in Quanzhou, and after drinking them you still say your lips were not wet. Xuanjue said: In what place did they give him wine to drink.

text_zh: 鏡清問。清虛之理。畢竟無身時如何。師曰。理 即如此。事作麼生。鏡清云。如理如事。師曰。 謾曹山一人即得。爭奈諸聖眼何。鏡清云。若 無諸聖眼。爭鑑得箇不恁麼。師曰。官不容針。 私通車馬大溈哲云。曹山雖然善能切磋琢磨。其奈鏡清玉本無瑕。要會麼。不經敏手。終成廢器。
text_en: it is just so. But in actual fact, how is it? Jingqing said, As in principle, so in fact. The master said, You may fool Caoshan alone, but what will you do about the eyes of the sages? Jingqing said, If there were no eyes of the sages, how could one discern this not-so? The master said, In public office a needle is not allowed; in private, carts and horses pass through. Dawei Zhe said: Although Caoshan was good at cutting, polishing, and refining, Jingqing’s jade was originally without flaw. If you want to understand, without a skilled hand it will in the end become a ruined vessel.

text_zh: 師問德上座。菩薩在定。聞香象渡河。出甚麼 經。僧云。出涅槃經。師曰。定前聞。定後聞。僧 云。和尚流也。師曰。道也太殺道。始道得一 半。僧云。和尚如何。師曰。灘下接取。
text_en: sutra does this come? The monk said, It comes from the Nirvāṇa Sutra. The master said, Did he hear before samādhi or after samādhi? The monk said, master, you are drifting. The master said, You talk far too much; you have only spoken half of it. The monk said, Then how about you, master? The master said, Catch it below the rapids.
The paper-robed Daoist came to consult. The master asked, Are you not the paper-robed Daoist? He said, I dare not.

text_zh: 紙衣道者來參。師問。莫是紙衣道者否。云不 敢。師曰。如何是紙衣下事。道者云。一裘纔挂 體。萬法悉皆如。師曰。如何是紙衣下用。道者 近前應諾。便立脫。師曰。汝秖解恁麼去。何不 解恁麼來。道者忽開眼問云。一靈真性。不假 胞胎時如何。師曰。未是妙。道者云。如何是 妙。師曰。不借借。道者珍重便化。師示頌曰。 覺性圓明無相身。莫將知見妄疎親。念異便 於玄體昧。心差不與道為隣。情分萬法沈前 境。識鑒多端喪本真。如是句中全曉會。了然 無事昔時人。
text_en: The master said, What is the matter beneath the paper robe? The Daoist said, As soon as a single cloak is hung on the body, the ten thousand dharmas are all thus. The master said, What is the function beneath the paper robe? The Daoist stepped forward, answered, and immediately died standing. The master said, You only know how to go like this. Why not know how to come like this? The Daoist suddenly opened his eyes and asked, The one numinous true nature, without relying on womb and fetus, what is it then? The master said, That is not yet the marvelous. The Daoist said, What is the marvelous? The master said, Not borrowing, and yet borrowing. The Daoist bade farewell and passed away. The master presented a verse and said: The awakened nature, perfectly bright, is the formless body. Do not, through views and knowledge, vainly divide distant and near. When thought differs, then the mysterious essence is obscured. When the mind deviates, it no longer neighbors the Way. Feeling divides the ten thousand dharmas, sinking into objects before it; discriminating consciousness reflects in many ways and loses the original truth. If within these lines you wholly understand and meet it, then clearly you are the person of old with nothing to do.
A monk cited Minister Lu Geng asking Nanquan, What is your surname? Nanquan said, Surname Wang.

text_zh: 僧舉陸亘大夫問南泉。姓甚麼。南泉曰。姓王。 亘云。王還有眷屬也無。南泉曰。四臣不昧。亘 云。王居何位。南泉曰。玉殿苔生。問師。玉殿 苔生意旨如何。師曰。不居正位。僧云。八方來 朝時如何。師曰。他不受禮。僧云。何用來朝。 師曰。違則斬。僧云。違是臣分上。未審君意如 何。師曰。樞密不得旨。僧云。恁麼則爕理之 功。全歸臣相也。師曰。爾還知君意麼。僧 云。外方不敢論量。師曰。如是如是。
text_en: Geng said, Does the king still have attendants or not? Nanquan said, The four ministers are not obscured. Geng said, In what position does the king dwell? Nanquan said, Moss grows in the jade hall. He asked the master, The jade hall overgrown with moss, what is its meaning? The master said, He does not dwell in the central position. The monk said, When the eight directions come to court, what then? The master said, He does not accept their homage. The monk said, Then what is the use of coming to court? The master said, Disobey, and they are beheaded. The monk said, Disobedience belongs to the ministers' side; I still do not know the ruler's intent, what is it? The master said, The privy council has not received the command. The monk said, If so, then the work of ordering and regulating all belongs entirely to the ministers and chancellors. The master said, Do you know the ruler's intent or not? The monk said, One outside the court dares not discuss it. The master said, Just so, just so.
A monk asked, This student is sick all through his body. Please, master, heal me. The master said, I do not heal. The monk

text_zh: 僧問。學人通身是病。請師醫。師曰不醫。僧 云。為甚麼不醫。師曰。教汝求生不得。求死不 得。
text_en: said, Why do you not heal? The master said, To make it so you cannot seek life and cannot seek death .
A monk asked the master, An ancient said, I have a great illness, not something the world can heal. I wonder, what

text_zh: 僧問師。古人曰。吾有大病。非世所醫。未審是 甚麼病。師曰。攢簇不得底病。僧云。一切眾 生。還有此病也無。師曰。人人盡有。僧云。和 尚還有此病也無。師曰。正覓起處不得。僧云。 一切眾生。為甚麼不病。師曰。一切眾生若病。 即非眾生。僧云。未審諸佛還有此病也無。師 曰。有。僧云。既有。為甚麼不病。師曰。為伊惺 惺。
text_en: illness is this? The master said, The illness of not being able to gather it together. The monk said, Do all sentient beings have this illness or not? The master said, Everyone has it completely. The monk said, Does the master also have this illness or not? The master said, Right now I cannot even find where it begins. The monk said, Why are all sentient beings not ill? The master said, If all sentient beings were ill, then they would not be sentient beings. The monk said, I wonder whether the buddhas have this illness or not. The master said, They do. The monk said, Since they have it, why are they not ill? The master said, Because they are lucid, lucid.
A monk asked, Is not a śramaṇa one endowed with great compassion? The master said, Yes. The monk

text_zh: 僧問。沙門豈不是具大慈悲底人。師曰。是。僧 云。忽遇六賊來時如何。師曰。亦須具大慈悲。 僧云。如何具大慈悲。師曰。一劍揮盡。僧云。 盡後如何。師曰。始得和同。
text_en: said, If suddenly the six thieves come, then what? The master said, One must also have great compassion. The monk said, How does one have great compassion? The master said, With one sword, sweep them all away. The monk said, After sweeping them all away, then what? The master said, Only then is harmony attained.
A monk asked the master, Do the eyebrows and the eyes recognize each other or not? The master said, They do not recognize each other.

text_zh: 僧問師。眉與目。還相識也無。師曰。不相識。 僧云。為甚麼不相識。師曰。為同在一處。僧 云。恁麼則不分去也。師曰。眉且不是目。目 且不是眉僧云。如何是目。師曰。端的去。僧 云。如何是眉。師曰。曹山却疑。僧云。和尚為 甚麼却疑。師云。若不疑。即端的去也。
text_en: The monk said, Why do they not recognize each other? The master said, Because they are in the same place. The monk said, Then in that case they are not distinct. The master said, Eyebrows are not eyes, and eyes are not eyebrows. The monk said, What are eyes? The master said, Go straight to it. The monk said, What are eyebrows? The master said, Caoshan instead has doubts. The monk said, master, why do you instead doubt? The master said, If I did not doubt, I would go straight to it.

text_zh: 僧問。五位對賓時如何。師曰。汝即今問那箇 位。僧云。某甲從偏位中來。請師向正位中接。 師曰不接。僧云。為甚麼不接。師曰。恐落偏位 中去。師却問僧。秖如不接。是對賓。是不對 賓。僧云。早是對賓了也。師曰。如是如是。
text_en: position are you asking about right now? The monk said, I come from the partial position; I ask the master to receive me from the upright position. The master said, I do not receive you. The monk said, Why do you not receive me? The master said, For fear of falling into the partial position myself. The master then asked the monk, Tell me, this not receiving, is it facing the guest or not facing the guest? The monk said, It was already facing the guest. The master said, Just so, just so.

text_zh: 僧問。萬法從何而生。師曰。從顛倒生。僧云。 不顛倒時。萬法何在。師曰在。僧云。在甚麼 處。師曰。顛倒作麼。
text_en: When there is no inversion, where are the ten thousand dharmas? The master said, They are there. The monk said, Where are they? The master said, What are you doing upside down?

text_en: luckily you are a capable man. Why ask Caoshan again?

text_en: Do not distinguish forms. The monk said, Why not distinguish forms? The master said, If you distinguish forms, then you are deluded.

text_en: tell me, with so many people in Hongzhou city, where do they go.

The monk said, It is true enough that those who meet it all perish. But why does the head fall for one who does not meet it. The master said, Have you not heard it said, It can exhaust all things. The monk said, What is it like after all is exhausted. The master said, Only then do you know this sword is there.

text_en: is it shown. The master lifted up the tray.

text_zh: 僧問。幻本何真。師曰。幻本元真法眼別云。幻本不真僧云。 當幻何顯。師曰。即幻即顯法眼別云。幻即無當僧云。恁 麼則始終不離于幻也。師曰。覓幻相不可得。
text_en: Through illusion, how is it revealed. The master said, Illusion itself is the revealing. The master said, Seek the mark of illusion and it cannot be found.

text_en: said, Rabbit horns need not be called nonexistent. Ox horns need not be called existent.

text_en: What is the person who is always not present. The master said, Hard to come by.

text_en: said, What is the different. The master said, Can you fail to know pain and itch.

text_en: A monk asked, I have heard the ancients say, No one falls to the ground without relying on the ground to rise.

text_en: What is falling. The master said, Consent is it. The monk said, What is rising. The master said, Rising.

text_en: so. The monk said, Then where is the grace between father and son. The master said, Only then is the grace of father and son fulfilled. The monk said, What is the grace of father and son. The master said, Knives and axes cannot split it.

text_en: what then. The master said, Caoshan loves toppled wine.

text_en: The master said, It contains the ten thousand things. The monk said, Why does it not lodge a corpse. The master said, One without breath cannot attach. The master said, The ten thousand things are not its merit. Breath cut off has its own condition. The monk said, Above this, is there still any matter or not. The master said, To say there is or to say there is not is acceptable, but what can you do when the Dragon King presses his sword.

text_en: phrases. The monk said, Then what is there to challenge. The master said, Knives and axes cannot cut in. The monk said, In such questioning and challenging, is there anyone who does not assent. The master said, Yes. The monk said, Who is that person. The master said, Caoshan.

text_zh: 僧問。世間甚麼物最貴。師曰。死猫兒頭最貴。 僧云。為甚麼死猫兒頭最貴。師曰。無人著價。
text_en: The monk said, Why is a dead cat's head most precious. The master said, No one can set a price on it.

text_en: Where then is it revealed. The master said, Last night by the bedside, I lost three coins.
A monk asked, What is it like before the sun comes out. The master said, Caoshan too once came like that.

text_en: The monk said, What about after it comes out. The master said, Still half a month's journey short of Caoshan.

text_zh: 師問僧。作甚麼。僧云掃地。師曰。佛前掃。佛 後掃。僧云。前後一時掃。師曰。與曹山過靸鞋 來五祖戒。代僧語云。和尚是何心行。
text_en: The monk said, I sweep front and back at one time. The master said, Bring Caoshan his sandals to pass over to him here. Wuzu Jie, speaking for the monk, said: Master, what kind of mind-practice is this.

text_zh: 僧問。抱璞投師。請師雕琢。師曰。不雕琢。僧 云。為甚麼不雕琢。師曰。須知曹山好手。
text_en: said, Why do you not carve or polish. The master said, You must know Caoshan has good hands.

text_en: a single flower.

text_en: person is that. The master said, There must not be a second moon. The monk said, What is the second moon. The master said, Even so, elder brother, you must settle it yourself. The monk said, Then what is the first moon. The master said, Dangerous.

text_en: not a single drop of water may touch you.

text_en: Do not treat it lightly. If, at the point of undertaking, it is clear, then you can turn all the sages behind your own back, and only then gain freedom. If you cannot turn them, even if you have learned to full completion, you must still stand behind them with folded hands. What big talk can you make? If you can turn yourself, then when all coarse and heavy situations come, you can be master of them all. Suppose you fall to the ground in the mud; even then you can be master. For example, a monk asked Yaoshan, In the teachings of the Three Vehicles, is there still the Patriarch s meaning or not? He answered, There is. The monk said, Since there is, why then did Bodhidharma come? Yaoshan said, He came precisely because there is. Is this not being master and turning it back to oneself? As the sutra says, Great Penetrating Wisdom Victory Buddha sat at the seat of enlightenment for ten kalpas. The Buddha-Dharma did not appear before him, and he did not attain Buddhahood. Kalpa here means obstruction. This is called tenfold completion. It is also called cutting off leakages. It is only that the ten directions are cut off. Yet if one does not forget the great fruit, then this guarding and clinging is called casual undertaking, with no distinction of noble or base. I often see monasteries fond of discussing one kind and two kinds. Can they actually establish the matter? These are only words about what goes onward, a layout of the road. Have you not seen Nansen say: Even if you have tenfold completion, you still fall short of Master Wang by a single thread. This is indeed a difficult matter. At this point you must be very careful before clarity and ease can be attained. Whether heaven, hell, hungry ghosts, or beasts, in every place do not shift or change. Originally you are the same old person, only you do not walk the old road. If there is delighting mind, it again becomes attachment. If you can get free, what is there to choose? An ancient worthy said, Only fearing one may not obtain rebirth. Tell me, how is it? People nowadays, speaking of some pure and clean place, love to talk of what goes onward. This sickness is the hardest to cure. As for worldly coarse and heavy matters, those are actually light. The sickness of purity and cleanliness is heavy. Even Buddha-flavor and Patriarch-flavor are all attachments. My former teacher said, To stir the mind is breaking precepts. If you get a taste, that is breaking the fast. But what do you call taste? It is only Buddha-flavor and Patriarch-flavor. As soon as delighting mind appears, that is breaking precepts. If we speak now of breaking the fast and breaking precepts, then right now at the time of the three karmas of ordination, they are already broken. As for coarse greed, anger, and ignorance, though hard to cut off, they are still light. But if it is non-action, no affairs, purity and cleanliness, this is heavy beyond anything more. The Patriarchs came into the world only for this. It was not only for you. At present do not take it lightly. A black servant and a white ox practice faster. It is not because they have Chan or the Way. As for your various pursuits, seeking Buddha, seeking Patriarch, and even bodhi and nirvana, when will they ever rest and be accomplished? All of it is mind of arising and ceasing. Therefore they are not equal to the black servant and the white ox, dull and without knowing, not knowing Buddha, not knowing Patriarch, not even bodhi and nir- vana, nor good and evil, cause and effect. They only eat grass when hungry and drink water when thirsty. If you can be like this, do not worry that it will not be accomplished. Have you not seen it said: Calculation does not succeed; therefore one must know it is there. Then one can wear fur and horns, pull the plow and drag it along. Gaining this advantage, one only then comes a little closer. Have you not seen Maitreya, Akshobhya, and all the wondrous joyful worlds, which are by those who are beyond called shameless, lazy bodhisattvas? They are also called transformation- birth-and-death. That is still feared to be only small laziness. In the fundamental matter, how should it be? You very much must be careful before it can be so. Everyone has a ground of the sitting cloth. Even if a Buddha appears in the world, he cannot encroach on it. Practice and realize in this way; do not chase quick gain. If you want to know this matter, even if you are made into a Buddha or a Patriarch, it is only this. And if you fall into the three evil paths, hell, or the six destinies, it is only this. Although it seems of no use, still you cannot leave it. You must become its master. If you can be master, then there is no transformation or change. If you cannot be master, then it is transformation and change. Have you not seen Yongjia say, Vast and heedless, one invites calamity. A monk asked, What is vast and heedless inviting calamity? He said, This whole thing is exactly it. The monk asked, How can one avoid it? He said, Knowing it is there is enough. What use is avoidance? Bodhi, nirvana, affliction, ignorance, and the like are all not to be avoided. Even worldly coarse and heavy matters, just know they are there and that is enough. Do not avoid them. To avoid is to go along with transformation and change. Even becoming Buddha or Patriarch, bodhi and nirvana, these calamities are by no means small. Why is it thus? Only because of transformation and change. If there is no transformation and change, then one must be free at every point of contact.

text_zh: 上堂僧問。如何是大闡提人。師曰。不懼業。僧 云。如何是無明人。師曰。始終不覺悟。僧云。 此二人誰在前。師曰。無明者。僧云。闡提人為 什麼在後。師曰。向去者。僧云。恁麼則無明者 不從今日去也。師曰是。僧云。既不從今日去。 無明從何處來。師曰。光處不敢入。僧云。豈不 是不明不暗。師曰是。僧云。正恁麼時如何。師 曰。不受觸。師復曰。闡提有多種。一類者。是 殺父。殺母。出佛身血。破和合僧。毀壞伽藍。 此剋定實報受種種苦。一類者。亦所作如前。 此則為殺無明父貪愛母。不信有佛法僧可 破有伽藍可壞。計為業心所得。故墮亦受種 種虛妄果報。如前升降不同。一類者。知有自 己本來事。呼為父母。不因外得。無修無證。非 因非果。不因師受。不從證行所得。不起父 見曰殺。不起母見曰害。即是一切本分事不 取不存故曰殺害。纔有纖毫奉重。得味不成。 知有自己事也。故曰大闡提。以此動撥妙力。 即是從上宗乘體會家事承當。要截玄道破 諸迂曲。即如新豐老人所玄示也。
text_en: said, What is a person of ignorance? The master said, From beginning to end, not awakened. The monk said, Which of these two is prior? The master said, The ignorant one. The monk said, Why is the icchantika person behind? The master said, The one who goes on. The monk said, Then in that case, the ignorant one does not go on from today. The master said, Yes. The monk said, Since he does not go on from today, from where does ignorance come? The master said, It dares not enter the place of light. The monk said, Is that not neither bright nor dark? The master said, It is. The monk said, At just such a time, what then? The master He said, It does not receive contact. The master continued, Icchantikas are of many kinds. One kind is this: killing father, killing mother, drawing the Buddha's blood, breaking up the harmonious sangha, and destroying monasteries. Such ones are certainly bound to receive direct retribution and undergo many sufferings. Another kind also does as above, but here father means ignorance and mother means craving. They do not believe there is Buddha, Dharma, or Sangha to be broken, nor monasteries to be destroyed. They take all this as attained by karmic mind, and so they fall and also receive various false karmic fruits and retributions. As before, their rise and fall differ. Another kind knows there is one's own original matter, and calls that father and mother. It is not obtained from outside, with no cultivation and no realization, neither cause nor effect, not received from a teacher, not gained through realization and practice. Not raising the view of father is called killing, and not raising the view of mother is called harming. This is all one's fundamental affair, not grasping and not preserving, therefore called killing and harming. If there is the slightest trace of cherishing or weighting it, savor cannot be realized. This is knowing there is one's own matter. Therefore it is called the great icchantika. With this one sets the subtle power in motion. This is precisely to embody and take responsibility for the family affair realized in the ancestral vehicle from above, to cut off the dark path and break through all crooked byways, just as the old man of Xinfeng obscurely indicated.
National Teacher Zhong suddenly called the attendant. The attendant came and stood there. The National Teacher lowered his head. The attendant

text_zh: 忠國師驀喚侍者。侍者來立。國師低頭。侍者 立多時出去。國師喚侍者。如是三度了曰。將 謂我辠負汝。汝却辠負我。百丈舉問趙州。國 師三喚侍者意作麼生。州曰。如人暗裏書字。 字雖不成。文彩已彩。又後有人。舉問師。國師 三喚侍者意作麼生。師曰。侍者第二遍回來。 云某甲不信和尚喚。
text_en: stood a long while and went out. The National Teacher called the attendant again. After doing this three times, he said, I had thought I was letting you down, but instead you are letting me down. Baizhang cited this and asked Zhaozhou, The National Teacher calling the attendant three times, what was his meaning. Zhaozhou said, It is like a man writing characters in the dark. Though the characters are not formed, the patterning is already there. Later someone again cited it and asked the master, The National Teacher calling the attendant three times, what was his meaning. The master said, When the attendant came back the second time, he said, I do not believe the master was calling me.
Nanquan said, Before one has a formed embryo, is there speech or not. Someone cited this and asked

text_zh: 南泉曰。未具胞胎時。還有語也無。有人舉問 雪峯。峯曰。道有道無。則喫三十棒。又問招 慶。慶曰。從他自道。又舉問師。師曰。有。云請 和尚傍瞥。師曰。將什麼物聞。云聾者還聞也 無。師曰。聾者若得聞。則具耳目。云什麼人得 聞。師曰。未具胞胎者。
text_en: Xuefeng. Xuefeng said, Say there is or say there is not, and you get thirty blows. Then he asked Zhaoqing, and Qing said, Let him speak for himself. He also cited it and asked the master. The master said, There is. He said, Please, Master, give a side glance. The master said, With what thing do you hear. He said, Can the deaf still hear or not. The master said, If the deaf could hear, then they would possess ears and eyes. He said, What person can hear. The master said, One not yet formed in the womb.
A monk asked the master, The teachings say a single phrase can swallow hundreds of thousands of meanings. What is that

text_zh: 僧問師。教云。一句能吞百千萬義。如何是一 句。師曰。針剳不入。
text_en: one phrase. The master said, Even a needle cannot pierce it.
There was a lecture master taking leave of Nanquan. Quan asked, Where are you going. He replied, Down the mountain.

text_zh: 有一座主。辭南泉。泉問。什麼處去。對云。山 下去。泉曰。第一不得謗王老師。對云。爭敢謗 和尚。泉噴水曰。多少。座主便出去。師曰。賴 也。
text_en: Quan said, First of all, do not slander Teacher Wang. He replied, How would I dare slander the master. Quan spat out water and said, How much. The lecture master then went out. The master said, Good thing indeed.
One day Guishan called the head monk. The head monk came. Shan said, I called the head monk. Why did you

text_zh: 溈山一日喚院主。院主來。山曰。我喚院主。汝 來作什麼。院主無對。師代曰。也知和尚不喚 某甲。又令侍者喚第一座。第一座來。山曰。我 喚第一座。汝來作什麼。師代曰。若令侍者喚。 恐不來。
text_en: come. The head monk had no reply. The master answered on his behalf, I also know the master was not calling me. He then had the attendant call the first seat. The first seat came. Shan said, I called the first seat. Why did you come. The master answered on his behalf, If he had the attendant call, I feared he would not come.
A monk took leave of Yaoshan to return home. Yaoshan asked, There is a man, his whole body red and raw,

text_zh: 有僧。辭藥山歸鄉去。藥山問。有一人。遍身紅 爛。臥在荊棘之中。僧云。恁麼則學人不歸去。 藥山曰。但知歸去。與爾休糧方。問如何是休 糧方。山曰。每日上堂不咬破一粒米也。師曰。 只如古德有云遍身紅爛底人。秖是醜陋底 人。一切人近不得。無拈掇處。更道臥在荊棘 之中。只道在如今日用。也亦無作拈掇處護 持保任邊事。時有僧問師。遍身紅爛時如何。 師曰。荷負。云荷負什麼人。師曰。勿紅爛到闍 黎。又問。醜陋人與滿身紅爛底人。阿那個是 重。師曰。大醜陋底人重。師又舉問僧。大保任 底人保任個什麼。自代曰。終日在背後。不曾 覰著。
text_en: lying among thorns. The monk said, If so, then this student will not go home. Yaoshan said, Just know to go home, and I will give you the method of fasting. He asked, What is the fasting method. Shan said, Each day when ascending the hall, do not bite through a single grain of rice. The master said, As for the ancient worthy who said the man with the whole body red and raw is simply the ugly man, no one can approach him, with no place to take hold. And further he said he lies among thorns. This only speaks of present daily use. There too there is no place to make a handle of it, nor of guarding and preserving it as a matter of maintenance. At that time a monk asked the master, What about when the whole body is red and raw. The master said, Carry it. He said, Carry whom. The master said, Do not let the redness and rawness reach you, Reverend. He again asked, Between the ugly man and the man all over red and raw, which one is weightier. The master said, The greatly ugly man is weightier. The master also brought this up and asked a monk, The greatly maintaining man, what does he maintain. He answered for him, All day it is behind his back; he has never once glanced at it.
Whenever master Juzhi was questioned, he only raised one finger. Later there was a novice who, when

text_zh: 俱胝和尚凡有詰問。唯舉一指。後有童子。因 外人問。和尚說何法要。童子亦竪起一指。胝 聞遂以刃斷其指。童子負痛號哭而去。胝復 召之。童子回首。胝却竪起指。童子忽然領悟。 胝將順世。謂眾曰。吾得天龍一指頭禪。一生 用不盡。言訖而寂。師曰。俱胝承當處莾鹵。只 認得一機一境。
text_en: an outsider asked, What essential teaching does the master preach, likewise held up one finger. Zhi heard of it and thereupon cut off his finger with a blade. The novice, bearing the pain, cried out and ran away. Zhi then called him back. The novice turned his head. Zhi again raised his finger, and the novice suddenly understood. As Zhi was about to pass away, he told the assembly, I obtained Tianlong's one-finger Zen. In a whole lifetime I could not exhaust its use. Having said this, he passed in silence. The master said, Where Juzhi took it up was crude and rough. He only recognized one function and one circumstance.
Dongshan ascended the hall and said, The Way without mind accords with man; man without mind accords with the Way. If you wish to know the meaning within this,

text_zh: 洞山上堂。道無心合人。人無心合道。欲識個 中意。一老一不老。後僧舉問師。如何是一老。
text_en: one is old and one is not old. Later a monk cited this and asked the master, What is the old one.
The master said, Not propped up. He said, What is the not old one. The master said, A dead tree.

text_zh: 師曰。不扶持。云如何是一不老。師曰。枯木。
text_en: A monk asked the master, Vimalakirti remained silent and Manjushri praised it as excellent. I wonder whether that truly matched Vimalakirti's

text_zh: 僧問師。維摩默然文殊讚善。未審還稱得維 摩意麼。師曰。爾還縛得虛空麼。僧云。恁麼則 不稱維摩意也。師曰。他又爭肯。僧云。畢竟有 何所歸。師曰。若有所歸。即同彼二公也。僧云。 和尚又作麼生。師曰。待爾患維摩病始得。
text_en: intent. The master said, Can you bind empty space. The monk said, If so, then it did not match Vimalakirti's intent. The master said, And why would he agree to that. The monk said, In the end, is there any place of return. The master said, If there is a place of return, then it is the same as those two gentlemen. The monk said, then how about master. The master said, Wait until you suffer Vimalakirti's illness, then it can be discussed.
Dongshan came to Bishu. Bi asked, What have you come for. Shan said, To draw near the master.

text_zh: 洞山到椑樹。椑問曰。來作什麼。山云。親近和 尚。椑曰。若是親近。用動兩片皮作麼。山無 對。師曰。一子親得。僧問洞山。三身之中。阿 那身不墮眾數。山曰。吾常于此切。僧問師。先 師道。吾常于此切。意作麼生。師曰。要頭便斫 去。
text_en: Bi said, If it is truly drawing near, what use is there in moving two pieces of skin. Shan had no reply. The master said, One son personally got it. A monk asked Dongshan, Among the three bodies, which body does not fall into enumeration. Shan said, Here I am always keenly pressed. A monk asked the master, Formerly the teacher said, Here I am always keenly pressed. What was his meaning. The master said, If you want a head, then chop it off at once.
As Dongshan was about to enter final stillness, he told the assembly, I have an idle name in the world. Who can

text_zh: 洞山將圓寂。謂眾曰。吾有間名在世。誰人為 吾除得。眾皆無對。時沙彌出曰。請和尚法號。 山曰。吾間名已謝。師曰。從古至今。無人辨 得。
text_en: remove it for me. The assembly had no reply. Then a novice stepped forward and said, Please, master, your Dharma name. Shan said, My idle name has already fallen away. The master said, From ancient times until now, no one has discerned it.
While Wuzhu was drinking tea, Manjushri picked up a glass cup and asked, Is there still this in the South

text_zh: 無著喫茶次。文殊拈起玻璃盞問。南方還有 這箇麼。著曰無。文殊曰。尋常將什麼喫茶。著 無對。師代曰。久承大士按劍。為什麼處在一 塵。
text_en: or not. Zhu said, No. Manjushri said, What do you ordinarily use to drink tea. Zhu had no reply. The master answered on his behalf, For a long time I have received the Great Being pressing his sword; why is he dwelling in a mote of dust at all.
The master said, Before Dipankara there are two kinds. One does not yet know there is, like milk mixed with blood.

text_zh: 師曰。謂然燈前有二種。一未知有。同於類血 之乳。一知有。猶如意未萌時得本物。此名然 燈前。一種知有。往來言語聲色是非亦不屬 正照用。亦不得記。同類血之乳。是漏失邊事。 此名然燈後。直是三際事盡。表裏情忘。得無 間斷。此始得名正然燈。乃云得記。
text_en: One knows there is, as if obtaining the original thing before intention has sprouted. This is called before Dipankara. One kind of knowing there is, amid coming and going, words and speech, sounds and forms, right and wrong, still does not belong to correct illuminating function, and likewise does not receive prediction. It is like milk mixed with blood, an affair on the side of leakage and loss. This is called after Dipankara. It is simply that the affairs of the three times are exhausted, inner and outer feelings forgotten, and one attains no interruption. Only then is it rightly named Dipankara, and thus said to have received prediction.

text_zh: 解釋洞山五位顯訣
text_en: Explanation of Dongshan's Manifest Key to the Five Positions As for what the late master clarified regarding bias and upright, and the combined carrying, and the like, the intent was that of the late master himself. It was not to explain ranks of merit and progressive cultivation, nor to mix in scriptural phrases. It is simply a profound discussion outside the standard pattern, aiming at the most subtle meaning. It only clarifies the original substance handed down from above,

text_zh: 夫先師所明偏正與兼帶。等用先師本意。不為明功進修之位兼涉教句。直是格外玄談要絕妙旨。秖明從上物體 現前。冥叶古聖之道。今見諸學士詮揀先師意度。似有誤彰。不免聊為敘其差。當媿在不混其功。於中或有借位明 功借功明位。緣緒多端。功在臨時。看語來勢。不負來機。妙在佳致爾。
text_en: present before us, silently tallying with the way of the ancient sages. Now I see various scholars interpreting and selecting the late master’s intent, and it seems they have displayed it wrongly. I cannot avoid briefly describing their errors. I should be ashamed if I mix up its functions. Among these there are cases of borrowing a rank to clarify merit, and borrowing merit to clarify a rank. The threads of conditions are many. The function lies in the moment at hand. One must watch the momentum with which the words come, not fail the arriving opportunity. The subtlety lies only in fitting grace. 。

From the upright position one turns to the partial. Distinguishing it within the partial, this completes both meanings. When the upright rank turns toward the biased, it is because it does not confront things. Though it does not confront

text_zh: 正位却偏。就偏辨得。是圓兩意正位却偏者。為不對物。雖不對 物。却具　正中無用為偏。全用為圓。是兩意。問如何是全。云不顧者得底人也。此正位不明來也。若佛出世也恁 麼。若佛不出世也恁麼。所以千聖萬聖皆歸正位承當　正中偏却具此一位。第一不得動著　如學士揀獨脫物 外。起眾聖之前。云是正位却圓。其實屈正位也。此例語是古人道過跡尚存。猶未得語中無語。此復呼為非正位 也。為語中有語故。此可呼為有病兼帶。不得呼為相兼帶來耳。
text_en: things, still it fully possesses them. In the upright, no function is called biased; full function is called complete. These are two meanings. If asked what full means, it is said: a person who attains without looking back. This is the upright rank not made explicit as coming forth. If a Buddha appears in the world, it is just thus; if a Buddha does not appear in the world, it is also just thus. Therefore thousands of sages and myriads of sages all return to bearing responsibility in the upright rank. In the upright with bias, this rank is still present. First of all, it must not be stirred. If scholars select the solitary release outside things, arising before the many sages, and say this is the upright rank yet complete, in truth they have bent the upright rank. This type of saying is where the ancients spoke and traces still remain; it still has not reached no words within words. This is instead called not the upright rank, because there are words within the words. This may be called a flawed combined carrying. It must not be called combined carrying coming forth.
Though the partial position is partial, it also completes both meanings. Distinguished within conditions, this is no speech within speech.

text_zh: 偏位雖偏。亦圓兩意。緣中辨得。是有語中無 語為用處不立的。不立的則真不常用也　偏位雖偏亦圓者。用中無物不觸。是兩意雖就用中明。為語中不 傷。此乃竟日道如不道一般。又曰。偏位却圓。亦具緣中不觸。
text_en: no speech. For at the point of function nothing is fixed. If nothing is fixed, then the true is not a constant function. As for the biased rank being biased yet also complete, in function there is nothing it does not touch. These are two meanings. Though clarified within function, in the words it does not wound anything. This is talking all day as if not talking at all. It is also said: the biased rank yet complete, and it also possesses not touching within conditions.
Or there are those who come from within the upright position; this is speech within no speech. Coming within the upright does not combine with conditions. As when Yaoshan

text_zh: 或有正位中來者。是無語中有語正中來者。不兼緣。如藥山 曰。我有一句子。未曾向人說。道吾曰。相隨來也。此是他妙會得。如湖南觀察使語。此例甚多。事須合出不得混尊 卑。呼為無語中有語。又我有一句子。未曾向人說。此問答家。須就出不得乖角。乖角則不知有故　句句無語不 立尊貴。不落左右。故云正中來也　正位來。明正位不涉緣。又引語例者。如黑豆未生芽時作麼生。又如曰有一人 無出入息。又曰未具胞胎時還有言句也無。十方諸佛出身處也。此例喚作無語中有語　又有借事。正位中來者。 此一位答家。須向偏位中。明其體物。不得入正位明也。此一句要知。如先師問新羅僧。未過海時在什麼處。無 對。自代曰。秖今過海。也在什麼處。又如先師代慎微長老出拄杖語曰。如今出也有人辨得麼。此例雖緣中認得。 不同向去。辨不得。恐後人收落功勳。將為向上事　如諸學士揀問祖師意。答待特牛生兒則向汝道。曰此是正位 中來。此一例語切不得呼為正位中來。可曰玄學路中問答。俱然也別是一路。又不得呼為相兼帶。為顯明故。縱 賓主回互秖得呼為有病兼帶。
text_en: said, I have a phrase I have never spoken to anyone. Daowu said, It comes along together. This was his subtle understanding. As in the saying to the Hunan Inspector, there are many such examples. In such matters one must bring them out properly and not confuse higher and lower. This is called words within no words. Again, I have a phrase I have never spoken to anyone. In such question and answer, it must come out fittingly and not at odd angles. If it goes askew, then one does not know what is there. Every phrase is no words, and does not establish exaltedness, and does not fall to either side. Therefore it is called coming within the upright. Coming in the upright rank clarifies that the upright rank does not involve conditions. Further examples are cited, such as: before the black beans sprout, how is it. Or: there is one person with no outgoing or incoming breath. Or: before having a formed womb, are there words or not. And: the place from which the Buddhas of the ten directions emerge. Such examples are called words within no words. There are also cases of borrowing an occasion. As for coming within the upright rank, in this rank, the one answering must clarify its embodied thingness within the biased rank. One must not clarify it by entering the upright rank. This point must be understood. For example, the late master asked a Silla monk, Before crossing the sea, where were you. There was no reply. He himself answered in place: Right now, having crossed the sea, where are you. Or as when the late master spoke for Elder Shenwei in the staff matter, saying: Now that it is brought out, is there anyone who can discern it. Though in such examples it is recognized within conditions, it is not the same as going onward. If one cannot distinguish this, I fear later people will gather it into merit and take it for the matter above. For example, scholars classify the question, What was the patriarch’s meaning, and the answer, Wait until a gelded ox gives birth and then I will tell you, and say this is coming within the upright rank. This kind of saying absolutely must not be called coming within the upright rank. It may be called a question and answer on the road of dark learning, both so, yet it is a different path. It also must not be called combined carrying, because it is too explicit. Even if host and guest alternate and interpenetrate, it can only be called flawed combined carrying.
Or there are those who come from within the partial position; this is no speech within speech. Coming within the biased rank then combines with conditions. As when it is said:

text_zh: 或有偏位中來者。是有語中無語偏位中來者。則兼緣。如曰 即今底呼作什麼即得。無對。先師自代曰。不得不得。此例亦多。喚為有語中無語也　語從四大聲色中來。不立 處所是非。故曰緣中辨得是偏位中來也。引語例者。如曰什麼物恁麼來。亦曰光境俱忘復是何物。亦曰定慧等學 明見佛性。此例亦多。喚作有語中無語　偏位中來者。就物明體。如曰什麼物恁麼來。又光境俱忘。復是何物。此 一例語寄功明位。亦是余舊舉例。什麼物恁麼來。此一例語雖緣中認得。不同向去。又定慧等學明見佛性。此理如 何。此一例語亦余初舉例語。又如光境俱忘。為是教中之則。不同玄學。只要於他教則出宗門中。玄學外事也　秖 如出息不依眾緣。入息不居蘊界而住。此語全是功不同緣中認得。亦是予舊舉例。主家抽入正位。云有一人無出 入息。令渠知有正位　更有挾功極則淨潔位。亦得呼為偏位中來。此難辨。須揀得出　如學士揀僧問先師。如何 是玄旨。師曰。如死人舌。又問。十二時中將何奉獻。曰無物。曰是偏位中來。此二例語不得呼為偏位中來。須各 揀。若是玄旨一例語。可同於功勳也。此二例語并不得呼為偏位及兼帶也。前已明破了。是借功明位。借位明功。 同於此也。
text_en: What should this right now be called for it to be right. No reply. The late master answered in place himself: No, no. There are many such examples. This is called no words within words. Speech comes from the sounds and forms of the four elements, yet does not establish location, right or wrong. Therefore, if it is discerned within conditions, it is called coming within the biased rank. Examples include: What thing comes thus. Also: when both light and object are forgotten, what thing is it then. Also: cultivate concentration and wisdom equally to clearly see Buddha nature. There are many such examples. They are called no words within words. Coming within the biased rank clarifies the substance by means of things, as in What thing comes thus, and when both light and object are forgotten, what thing is it then. This kind of saying uses merit to clarify the rank, and is also an old example I gave. What thing comes thus. Though this example is recognized within conditions, it is not the same as going onward. Again, cultivate concentration and wisdom equally to clearly see Buddha nature. As for this principle, how is it. This too was an example I first raised. Again, both light and object forgotten is a rule from the teachings; it is not the same as dark learning. One only wants, from within those doctrinal rules, to bring out what in the school is a matter outside dark learning. Only as in, the outgoing breath does not rely on the many conditions, the incoming breath does not dwell in the aggregates and realms. This saying is entirely about merit and is not the same as recognition within conditions. It too is an old example I gave. The host side draws it into the upright rank, saying there is one person with no out- going or incoming breath, making him know there is an upright rank. There is also the pure and clean rank at the extreme of carried merit, which can also be called coming within the biased rank. This is hard to distinguish and must be sorted out. For example, scholars classify a monk asking the late master, What is the dark meaning. The master said: Like the tongue of a dead man. He also asked: Through the twelve hours, what should one offer. He said: Nothing. They say this is coming within the biased rank. These two examples must not be called coming within the biased rank. Each must be distinguished separately. As for the dark meaning example, it may be grouped with merit. These two examples together must not be called the biased rank nor combined carrying. This has already been clearly refuted earlier. They are borrowing merit to clarify rank, and borrowing rank to clarify merit. It is the same as this.

text_zh: 或有相兼帶來者。這裏不說有語無語。這裏 直須正面而去。這裏不得不圓轉。事須圓轉 相兼帶來者。為語勢不偏不正。不存不無。如全不全。似虧不虧。唯得正面而去也。去則不立的。不立的則至妙之 言。境不圓常情之事。如先師代文殊喫茶語。曰借取這箇看得麼。亦如翠微曰每日噇什麼。
text_en: one must go straight on from the front. Here one cannot but turn round and complete it. The matter must turn round completely. 。 Combined carrying coming forth means the force of the words is neither biased nor upright, neither existent nor nonexistent, like complete yet not complete, like lacking yet not lacking. One only gets the direct face and goes on. If it goes on, then nothing is fixed. If nothing is fixed, then the utmost subtle speech is not a matter rounded out by ordinary feeling. For example, the late master speaking in place in the Wenshu tea-drinking saying said: Borrow this and see, can you. Also like Cuiwei saying: What do you eat every day.
Yet words spoken along the way are altogether sickness. As for the person concerned, he must first discern words and phrases.

text_zh: 然在途之語。總是病。夫當人先須辨得語句。 正面而去。有語是恁麼來。無語是恁麼去。作 家中不無言語。不涉有語無語。這個喚作兼 帶語。兼帶語全無的的也相兼帶來者。不落有語無語。如藥山帶刀 語。此是兼帶語臨時看語來勢。或當頭正面而去。或異中虛。此若不妙會。則千里萬里也　引相兼帶來語例者。如 文殊喫茶語。及這個人如今什麼處去也。雲巖曰。作麼作麼。又曰。即今作麼生。此例甚多　亦有功勳中兼帶。似 向上事。臨時辨取。如落淨妙之處。則須知有事在。要去則去。要止則止。千萬宛轉不得莾鹵。夫問答兩家語勢 相報。皆不出五位也。但語有麁細。答有淺深。所以先師於非言句中。強以言。皆為對緣。而設斯要耳。如大無明 底人。為全體。不同闡提。闡提則知有事却鞔雖鞔却成孝養。鞔者不存祖佛及自己本分父母也。紅爛底人為不 歸全擔荷不立至尊。大保任底人為刺脚入泥裡。非小小護持　夫相兼帶來者。直須似文殊喫茶語。及先師答雲 巖鉏薑語。并安和尚法堂語。及藥山淳布衲洗佛語。於中最妙兼帶。無過藥山答道吾帶刀語。及百丈下堂大眾欲 散未散時問云。是什麼。藥山遙聞此語。云在此。便道暗頭兼帶。借功明物。借物明功。借過明功。借功明過。等來 若是。藥山與新豊并前諸德所出超過入正位。是玄談奇特句已。次到小小得力者。則抽入正位。此例語。常用 也。吾緣住持多緒。不及子細。略明少分許。汝等諸人。不須容易輕慢。若更有凝滯。旋當決了。直須勵力修行。 令未來際不斷此事。不得慢洩。或值純朴者。是奇器。亦不可隱耳。
text_en: Go straight on from the front. Speech comes in this way; no speech goes in this way. In a true adept's house there is not an absence of words, yet it does not involve speech or no speech. This is called integrated speech. Integrated speech is wholly without fixed marks. Combined carrying coming forth does not fall into words or no words, as in Yaoshan’s belt-knife saying. This is combined-carrying speech. At the moment one must watch the momentum of the words as they come. Sometimes it goes straight ahead face to face, sometimes there is emptiness within difference. If this is not subtly understood, one will be off by a thousand or ten thousand miles. Examples of combined carrying coming forth include the Wenshu tea-drinking saying, and This person now, where has he gone. Yunyan said: How, how. Also: Right now, how is it. There are many such examples. There is also combined carrying within merit, which seems like the matter above. It must be discerned on the spot. If it falls into a pure and subtle place, one must know there is still a matter there. If it should go, then go; if it should stop, then stop. In all the many turnings one must not be crude. As for the momentum of speech in questioning and answering on both sides, in their mutual response, none goes outside the five ranks. It is only that some speech is coarse or fine, and some answers shallow or deep. Therefore the late master, within what is not verbal phrases, forced it into words, all for responding to conditions and setting forth these essentials. For example, a person of great ignorance is the whole body, unlike an icchantika. An icchantika knows there is something, yet covers it over; though covered over, it still becomes filial support. To cover over means not preserving the patriarchs and Buddhas and one’s own original father and mother. The person red and rotting is one who does not return to the whole and bear it fully, and does not set up the supreme. The person of great preserving and maintaining is one whose feet are pricked and enter the mud, not someone of petty maintenance. As for combined carrying coming forth, it must be like the Wenshu tea-drinking saying, and the late master’s answer to Yun- yan’s ginger-hoeing saying, and Master An’s Dharma hall saying, and Yaoshan Chun the patched-robe monk washing Buddha saying. Among these, the most subtle combined carrying is none beyond Yaoshan’s answer to Daowu’s belt-knife saying, and Baizhang descending from the hall when the assembly was about to disperse but had not yet dispersed, and someone asked: What is this. Yaoshan, hearing these words from afar, said: Here it is. Then one can speak of hidden-side combined carrying, using merit to clarify the thing, using the thing to clarify merit, using excess to clarify merit, using merit to clarify excess, and so on. As for the sayings put forth by Yaoshan, Xinfeng, and the various earlier worthies, they surpass and enter the upright rank. These are already marvelous and extraordinary phrases of profound discourse. Next, when it comes to those of only slight attainment, they are drawn into the upright rank. This type of saying is commonly used. As for me, because the affairs of abbacy are many, I cannot be detailed, and have only briefly clarified a small portion. All of you people should not lightly slight this. If there are further hesitations and blockages, they should be resolved at once. You must exert yourselves in practice. Make this matter unbroken into the endless future. Do not grow lax and let it leak away. If you encounter one who is pure and simple, that is a rare vessel, and it must not be concealed.

text_zh: 三等之墮
text_en: The Three Kinds of Falling When a śramaṇa takes food, there are three kinds of falling. Becoming a water buffalo is the śramaṇa's falling.

text_zh: 夫沙門取食。有三等墮。作水牯牛是沙門墮。 不受食是尊貴墮。不斷聲色是隨類墮。只墮 去是甚麼人分上事欲知則是入異類中。不認沙門邊事。所以古人權借水牯牛為 異類。祇是事上異類。非言語中異類。
text_en: Not receiving food is the noble falling. Not cutting off sounds and forms is the falling along with kinds. Simply to fall like this belongs to what sort of person? If you want to know, this is entering among different kinds. It does not acknowledge matters on the side of the śramaṇa. Therefore the ancients provisionally borrowed the water buffalo as a different kind. It is only a different kind in terms of affairs, not a different kind in language.
If it is the different kind within speech, then all coming and going words are kinds. Therefore

text_zh: 若是言語中異類。則是往來言語盡是類。所 以南泉道。智不到處切忌道著。道著則頭角 生。喚作如如。早是變也。直須向異類中行。如 今須向異中道取異中事。夫語中無語始得。 若是南泉病時有人問。和尚百年後向甚麼 處去。泉曰。我向山下檀。越家。作一頭水牯牛 去。云某甲擬隨和尚去。還得麼。泉曰。若隨 我。含一莖草來這個是沙門轉身語。所以道。汝擬近。含一莖草來。親近渠。是呼為無 漏始堪供養渠。
text_en: Nanquan said, Where wisdom does not reach, avoid speaking of it. If you speak of it, horns and head arise. To call it thusness is already a transformation. One must directly move among the different kinds. Now one must, within difference, speak and take up the matter within difference. Only when there is no speech in speech is it attained. When Nanquan was ill, someone asked, Reverend, after a hundred years where will you go? Nanquan said, I will go to the Yue family's place below the mountain and become a water buffalo. The monk said, I intend to follow you, Master. May I? Nanquan said, If you follow me, bring a stalk of grass in your mouth. This is the śramaṇa turning-body phrase. Therefore it is said: If you would approach, hold a single blade of grass in your mouth and come near him. This is called without leakage; only then are you fit to make offerings to him.

text_zh: 又曰。隨類墮者。祇今於一切聲色物物上。轉 身去不隨階級。喚作隨類墮。又曰。尊貴墮者。 法身法性是尊貴邊事。亦須轉却。是尊貴墮。 祇如露地白牛。是法身極則。亦須轉却免他 坐一色無辨處。並是稱斷供養邊事。欲須供 養。須得此食。所以無味之味。亦曰無漏是堪 供養。並餘觸污之食。非無漏解脫之食也。有 人問百丈。以何為食。曰無漏為食。雲巖曰。莫 將以味為供養。道吾曰。知有保任處。盡是供 養。

Someone asked Baizhang, What is taken as food? He said, The undefiled is food. Yunyan said, Do not take flavor as offering. Daowu said, Where one knows and preserves this, all is offering. Offering.

text_zh: 夫取正命食者。須具三種墮。時有僧問。被毛 戴角是甚麼墮。不斷聲色是甚麼墮。不受食 是甚麼墮。余曰。被毛戴角是沙門墮。不斷聲 色是隨類墮。不受食是尊貴墮。不受食尊貴 墮者。是本分事。知有不取。故曰尊貴墮。被毛 戴角沙門墮者。不執沙門邊事及諸聖報位 也。不斷聲色隨類墮者。為初心知有自己本 分事。回光時。擯出諸色聲香味觸法。得寧謐 則成功後不執六塵。墮而不昧。任之無礙。故 曰。外道六師是汝師。彼師所墮。汝亦隨墮。可 以食。食者則是正命食也。亦本分事也。祇是就 六根門頭見聞覺知。不被染污。呼為墮。不同 向前怕也。本分事猶不取。況其餘沙門取食有三種墮。作 水牯牛。是甚麼墮。代曰。不處正位。不揀其身。始喚作沙門墮。不斷聲色。是甚麼墮。代曰。凡情得盡。聖量亦忘。 聲色塵中不應更斷。乃可取食。是為隨類墮。又曰。彼師所墮。汝亦隨墮。乃可取食。沙門墮者。亦不無其行。亦不 無其間。雖有其間。常無其間。雖有其行。常無其行。其中此事切須知時節莫東西。
text_en: and bearing horns, what falling is that? Not cutting off sounds and forms, what falling is that? Not receiving food, what falling is that? I said, Wearing fur and bearing horns is the śramaṇa falling. Not cutting off sounds and forms is falling along with kinds. Not receiving food is the noble falling. The noble falling of not receiving food is one's fundamental matter. One knows it yet does not take it, therefore it is called the noble falling. Wearing fur and bearing horns, the śramaṇa falling, means not clinging to matters on the śramaṇa side nor to the reward-positions of the sages. As for not cutting off sounds and forms, the falling along with kinds, when a beginner first knows his own fundamental matter, in turning the light around he casts out forms, sounds, smells, tastes, touches, and dharmas, and attains stillness. But after the work is accomplished, he does not cling to the six dusts, falls yet is not darkened, and lets them be without obstruction. Therefore it is said, The six teachers of the outsiders are your teachers; where those teachers fall, you also fall along. This can be eaten. Such food is the food of right livelihood. It too is the fundamental matter. It is simply at the gates of the six faculties that seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing are not stained; this is called falling. It is not like the earlier fearfulness. One does not even take the fundamental matter, much less the rest. In a śramaṇa taking food there are three kinds of falls. To become a water buffalo, what fall is that? In place of an answer it is said: Not abiding in the correct rank, not selecting his body, this is first called the śramaṇa fall. Not cutting off sounds and forms, what fall is that? In place of an answer it is said: Ordinary feelings are exhausted, and saintly measure too is forgotten. Amid the dust of sounds and forms, one should not sever further; only then may one take food. This is called the fall of following the kind. It is also said: Where that teacher falls, you too fall along with him; only then may you take food. As for the śramaṇa fall, it is not that there is no conduct, nor is it that there is not no interval. Though there is interval, there is always no interval. Though there is conduct, there is always no conduct. In this matter, one must certainly know the proper time and not go east or west.

text_zh: 一者往來異類者。如今一切聲色言語階級 地位捨父逃逝。盡皆却向上祖。又得為異 類。又天堂地獄餓鬼畜生修羅等。皆是異類。 二者菩薩同異類者。先明自己然後却入生 死異類中攝他。已證涅槃之果。不捨生死類。 自利利他。願一切眾生皆成佛。從末後成佛。 所以大權菩薩若不先化眾生。己事無由得 成辦。故南泉曰。先過那邊知有。却來遮邊行 李。菩薩具六度萬行。教云。若有一眾生未度 者。吾終不成正覺。誓願無邊。眾生無邊。如是 行持。故名菩薩同異類。三者沙門異類者。 先知有本分事了。喪盡今時一切凡聖因果 功行。始得就體一般。名為獨立底人。亦名沙 門稱斷事。始得表裏情忘三世事盡。得無遺 漏。得名佛邊事。亦云一手指天地。亦云具大 沙門。轉却沙門穪斷邊事。不入諸聖報位。始 得名為沙門行。亦云沙門轉身。亦云披毛戴 角。亦喚作水牯牛。恁麼時節始得入異類。亦 云色類邊事。所以古人道。頭長三尺頸長二 寸。秖是這個道理。不得別會。四者宗門中異 類者。如南泉曰。智不到處。切忌道著。道著則 頭角生。喚作如如。早是變也。直須向異類中 行。道取異類中事。洞山曰。此事直須妙會。事 在其妙。體在妙處。余自道。此事直須虛一位 全無的的也。覿面兼帶始得若是。作家語不 偏不正。不有不無。呼為異類中虛此事。直須 作家橫身。逢木著木。逢竹著竹。須護觸犯。囑 囑囑囑有人問余。如何是異。曰我若向汝道。驢年得異否。所以有人問南泉。百年後向甚麼處去。泉 曰。山下檀越家作一頭水牯牛去。云某甲隨和尚去得否。泉曰。爾若隨我。含一莖草來。余曰。此水牯牛不同沙門 水牯牛。直須子細始得。不迷時候。
text_en: abandon the father and flee away, yet all turn back upward to the ancestor and thereby become different kinds. Also heaven, hell, hungry ghosts, animals, asuras, and the like are all different kinds. Second, the bodhisattva the same yet different kind: first clarify oneself, then enter among the different kinds of birth-and-death to gather and guide others. Though having realized the fruit of nirvana, one does not abandon the kinds of birth-and-death. Benefiting oneself and benefiting others, one vows that all beings become Buddhas, and oneself becomes Buddha at the very end. Therefore, if a great-functioning bodhisattva does not first transform sentient beings, his own matter has no way to be accomplished. Thus Nanquan said, First pass to that side and know there is something, then come back to this side and carry on the work. A bodhisattva possesses the six perfections and ten thousand practices. The teaching says, If even one being is not yet ferried across, I will never accomplish perfect awakening. The vows are boundless, beings are boundless. Practicing in this way, therefore it is called the bodhisattva same-yet-different kind. Third, the śramaṇa different kind: first know the fundamental matter, then utterly lose all present worldly and holy causes and effects, merits and practices. Only then does one become one with the substance itself. This is called a person who stands alone, also called a śramaṇa of cut-off concerns. Only then are inner and outer feelings forgotten, the affairs of the three times exhausted, and one attains no remainder, no leakage. This is called a matter on the Buddha side. It is also called pointing to heaven and earth with one hand, and also called possessing the great śramaṇa. Turning away even from the śramaṇa's side of cut-off matters, not entering the reward-positions of the sages, only then is it called śramaṇa practice. It is also called the śramaṇa turning the body, also called wearing fur and bearing horns, and also called a water buffalo. Only at such a time does one enter the different kinds. It is also called a matter on the side of form-kinds. Therefore the ancients said, The head is three feet long and the neck is two inches long. It is only this principle and must not be understood otherwise. Fourth, the different kind within the school gate: as Nanquan said, Where wisdom does not reach, avoid speaking of it. If you speak of it, then horns and head arise. To call it thusness is already change. One must directly move among the different kinds and speak the matter within the different kinds. Dongshan said, This matter must be subtly understood. The matter lies in subtlety; the substance lies in the subtle place. I myself say, In this matter one must empty out a position so that there is nothing fixed at all. Only when face to face there is integrated carrying can it be attained. If it is the speech of a genuine adept, it is neither biased nor correct, neither existent nor nonexistent. This is called emptying this matter within the different kinds. One must directly as a genuine adept set the body crosswise; on meeting wood, attach to wood; on meeting bamboo, attach to bamboo. One must guard against violation and offense. I entrust, entrust, entrust. Someone asked me, What is different kind? I said, if I tell you, will you attain it in a donkey year? Thus someone asked Nanquan, After a hundred years, where will you go? Quan said, To the patron family at the foot of the mountain, to become a water buffalo. He said, Can I follow the master? Quan said, If you would follow me, hold a single blade of grass in your mouth and come. I say: this water buffalo is not the same as the śramaṇa water buffalo. You must be very careful to get it, and not lose the time.
Asked, What is the different kind that goes and comes? I said, One does not yet know one has oneself. Then I also said:

text_zh: 問如何是往來異類。余曰。未知有自己。又曰。 一切言語聲色是非總是往來異類。云如何 是同中異類。余曰。不擇其身。云如何是被毛 戴角。余曰。不立觸淨。又非時答觸。即觸遇淨 即淨。云如何是宗門中異類。余曰。要頭則斫 將去洞山先師因僧問沙門行。先師答曰。頭長三尺頸長二寸。又問余。此意如何。余曰。勝句妙句。僧云。喚 什麼作勝句妙句。余曰。勝句妙句有三種。一者諸佛出世四十九年施設方便。十二分教。百千三昧。妙門箇箇穿 究。盡是勝句妙句。此是出世邊說。二者從凡入聖。洞達自己與佛無異。得無遺漏始得通身。始喚作一塵一念十 方婆伽梵一路涅槃門。到恁麼時節。不處正位。不擇其身。却入異類中。被毛戴角。無異念。故云一切物類比況 不得。諸佛諸祖計挍不成。所以古人道。沙門語不得將尺寸語與人。故喚作勝句妙句。此是色類邊語。三者一切所 有底物比不得。始呼為勝句妙句。所以古人道。千般比不得。萬物況不成。智者不能知。上根亦不識。亦曰。本 來無相似。故勝句妙句。勝句妙句者。天上人間測度不得底事。故古人曰。喚作超始終句。借此為語類邊說行。
text_en: All speech, sounds, forms, and rights and wrongs are altogether the different kind that goes and comes. He asked: What is the different kind within sameness? I said, It does not choose its body. He asked, What is furred and horned? I said, It does not set up contact and purity. Also, when asked about contact, I did not answer in the usual way: contact is just meeting purity, and purity is just purity. He asked, What is the different kind within the school? I said, If you want a head, then chop it off and take it away. The former master Dongshan, because a monk asked about the śramaṇa practice, answered: The head is three chi long, the neck two cun long. He further asked me, what is the meaning of this? I said, a supreme phrase, a wondrous phrase. The monk said, called what is a supreme phrase and wondrous phrase? I said: There are three kinds of supreme and wondrous phrases. First, when the buddhas appear in the world, for forty-nine years they establish expedients, the twelvefold teachings, hundreds of thousands of samadhis, wondrous gates each and every one penetrating through to the end. All of these are supreme and wondrous phrases. This is speech from the side of appearing in the world. Second, from ordinary to sage, thoroughly understanding that oneself is not different from Buddha, attaining no leakage and only then attaining whole-body penetration, this is first called in a single dust mote, in a single thought, the ten directions Bhagavans, one road to the nirvana gate. When it comes to such a time, one does not abide in the correct rank, does not choose one's body, but instead enters among different kinds, wearing fur and horns, with no different thought. Therefore it is said that all species and things cannot be compared or analogized. They cannot be matched; all buddhas and patriarchs cannot measure it out. Therefore the ancients said: In speaking of the śramaṇa, one must not use talk of measurements with people. Therefore it is called a supreme and wondrous phrase. This is language on the side of forms and kinds. Third, all that exists as a thing cannot be compared to it; only then is it called a supreme and wondrous phrase. Therefore the ancients said: A thousand comparisons do not match, ten thousand things cannot serve as analogy. The wise cannot know it, and those of highest capacity also do not recognize it. It is also said, originally there is no likeness. Therefore it is a supreme and wondrous phrase. A supreme and wondrous phrase is a matter that heaven and the human world cannot measure. Therefore the ancients said it is called the phrase beyond beginning and end. Borrowing this, one speaks in terms of the side of language and kinds.

text_zh: 稠布衲問。如何是色類。余曰。被毛戴角。云如 何是云語類。余曰。曹山只有一雙眉。又問。如 何是水牯牛。余曰。矇矇瞳瞳。云此意如何。余 曰。不知有天地。稠又舉。上座問雲居。先師 有言。自少養一箇兒子。頭長三尺頸長二寸。 如何是自少養得底兒子。居曰。日給難忘。云 如何是頭長三尺。居曰。不奈何。云如何是頸 長二寸。居曰。至今還奈何得否。云如何是日 給難忘。居曰。常在則是。云如何是常在。居 曰。不違背則是。云如何是不奈何。居曰。到恁 麼時甚麼人奈何得。云至今還奈何。此意如 何。居曰。三世諸佛不奈何。問余。如何是頭 長三尺頸長二寸。余曰。不是從來底事。云如 何是從來底事。余曰。喚作甚麼。問沙門行箇 甚麼行。余曰。畜生行。云如何是畜生行。余 曰。被毛戴角。云如何是沙門。余曰。物物不間 斷。云不間斷底事如何。余曰。始得行。云如何 是被毛戴角底人。余曰。不懼業。云為甚麼到 恁麼地。余曰。若不懼業。甚麼處不到。問從凡 入聖則不問。從聖人凡時如何。余曰。水牯牛。 云如何是水牯牛。余曰。矇矇瞳瞳。云此意如 何。余曰。但念水草。餘無所知。云成得箇甚麼 邊事。余曰。秖是箇逢草喫草。逢水飲水又曰。這箇 語有力。欲知有力。此人不執沙門邊事。亦不入諸聖報位便是入異類。是異類是被毛戴角。喚作沙門行。亦喚作沙 門行李處。亦喚作頭長三尺頸長二寸。欲知此意。到沙門行時。不欲將尺寸分親疎。不得說張三李四　又頭長三 尺者。只得從小至大今日功成。得到恁麼時。喚作勝句妙句。頸長二寸者。是不坐沙門位。亦不處諸聖報位。故為 頸長二寸。恁麼時不得說著稱與不稱。所以道。不將尺寸來向這裏思量也。雖然如此。猶是類邊事。須知有異類中 事。不見道。智不到處。不得說著。說著即頭角生。喚作如如。早是變也。須向異類中行。喚作虛一位。喚作覿面兼 帶。全無的的也。
text_en: What is the class of spoken words? I said, Caoshan has only one pair of eyebrows. He asked again, What is a water buffalo? I said, Dim and muddled. He asked, What does that mean? I said, It does not know there is heaven and earth. Chou then brought up another case: A senior monk asked Yunju, The former master once said, Since youth I have raised a son, his head three feet long and his neck two inches long. What is this son raised since youth? Ju said, Daily provision is hard to forget. He asked, What is the head three feet long? Ju said, Nothing can be done about it. He asked, What is the neck two inches long? Ju said, Even now, can anything be done about it? He asked, What is daily provision hard to forget? Ju said, It is just always there. He asked, What is always there? Ju said, It is just not turning away from it. He asked, What is nothing can be done about it? Ju said, When it comes to this point, who could do anything about it? He asked, Even now, can anything be done about it? What does this mean? Ju said, The Buddhas of the three times can do nothing about it. He then asked me, What is the head three feet long and the neck two inches long? I said, It is not the matter from the beginning. He asked, What is the matter from the beginning? I said, What do you call it? He asked, What practice does a śramaṇa practice? I said, The practice of beasts. He asked, What is the practice of beasts? I said, Furred and horned. He asked, What is a śramaṇa? I said, Not cut off from thing after thing. He asked, What about that which is unbroken? I said, Only then does one attain practice. He asked, What is the person who is furred and horned? I said, One who does not fear karma. He asked, Why does one reach such a place? I said, If one does not fear karma, where could one not arrive? He asked, I will not ask about going from ordinary to sage. But when going from sage to ordinary, how is it? I said, A water buffalo. He asked, What is a water buffalo? I said, Dim and muddled. He asked, What does this mean? I said, It thinks only of water and grass; of the rest it knows nothing. He asked, What sort of thing is accomplished thereby? I said, It is simply this: when it meets grass it eats grass, when it meets water it drinks water. It is also said, this phrase has power. If you wish to know power, this person does not cling to matters on the śramaṇa side, and does not enter the reward-ranks of the sages; this is precisely entering different kinds. This different kind is wearing fur and horns. It is called śramaṇa practice, and also called śra- maṇa baggage-place. It is also called the head three chi long and neck two cun long. If you wish to know this meaning, when arriving at śramaṇa practice, one does not wish to use measurements to divide near and far. One must not speak of Zhang San or Li Si. Further, head three chi means only that from small to great, today the work is accomplished. When one reaches such a time, it is called a supreme and wondrous phrase. Neck two cun means one does not sit in the śramaṇa rank, nor abide in the reward-ranks of the sages. Therefore it is called neck two cun long. At such a time one must not speak of fitting or not fitting. Therefore it is said: Do not bring measurements here to think about it. Even so, this is still a matter on the side of kinds. You must know there is within different kinds a matter. Have you not seen it said: Where wisdom does not reach, one must not speak of it. Speak of it and horns immediately grow on the head. To call it thusness is already a change. One must proceed within different kinds. This is called the empty single rank, called face-to-face inclusive carrying. It is entirely without anything fixed.

text_zh: 云如何是類。余曰。被毛戴角。云如何是異。余 曰。作麼作麼。云如何是行。余曰。要頭則斫將 去云只如異類。成得箇甚麼邊事。余曰。此事有二種異類。一者沙門異類。二者事上異類。事上異類者。狸 奴白牯是也。沙門異類者。觸處得自由。始得不變易。不同那箇。先師問余。甚麼處去。余曰。不變易處去。此不變 易事有二種。一者人人盡有本分事。二者知有底人。不捨一切聲色是非。於一切物物上不滯。呼為一切處不易。亦 喚作被毛戴角。亦喚作入泥入水。亦喚作行李底漢。
text_en: said, Doing this, doing that. He asked, What is practice? I said, If you want a head, then chop it off and take it away. He said, As for different kinds, what sort of matter does it accomplish? I said: In this matter there are two kinds of different kinds. First, śramaṇa different kind. Second, affair-level different kind. Affair-level different kind is the civet cat and white ox. Śramaṇa different kind means gaining freedom at every contact, and only then attaining non-change. It is not the same as that. The former master asked me, Where are you going? I said, To the place of non-change. This non-change matter has two kinds. First, everyone fully has the matter of their own share. Second, for a person who knows there is, he does not abandon any sounds, forms, rights, or wrongs, and is not obstructed upon any and every thing. This is called unchanging in every place. It is also called wearing fur and horns, also called entering mud and entering water, also called a fellow of baggage-carrying.
He asked, What is entering mud and entering water? The master said, No change. He asked, Is it turning the body or not?

text_zh: 云如何是入泥入水。師曰。不變易。云轉身也 否。余曰。不轉身。云此人屋裏事如何。余曰。 諸聖測不得。云為甚麼測不得。余曰。是伊不 同諸聖。云此猶是類邊事。還有向上事否。余 曰有。云如何是向上事。余曰。向汝道。則恐落 類邊去。
text_en: I said, It does not turn the body. He asked, What is this person's house-affair? I said, The sages cannot fathom it. He asked, Why can they not fathom it? I said, Because he is not the same as the sages. He asked, This is still a matter on the side of kinds. Is there also an upward matter? I said, There is. He asked, What is the upward matter? I said, If I tell you, I fear it will fall to the side of kinds.

text_zh: 正中來者太過也。全身獨露。萬法根源。無咎 無譽。偏中至者中孚也。隨物不礙。木舟中虛 虛通自在。正中偏者巽也。虛空破片處處圓 通。根塵寂爾。偏中正者兌也。水月鏡像本無 生滅。豈有蹤跡。兼中到者重離也。正不必虛。 偏不必實。無背無向。又曰。心機泯。色空忘。 更無覆藏。全體露現。是曰正中偏。山是山。水 是水。無人安名。無物比倫。是曰偏中正。淨 躶躶。赤洒洒。面目堂堂。盡天盡地。獨尊無 二。是曰正中來。宛如寰中天子。不借禹湯堯 舜令。眼見耳聞。終不借他力。耳之不入聲中。 聲之不塞耳根。裏頭才轉身。塵中未帶名。是 曰兼中至。不是心不是境。不是事。不是理。從 來離名狀。天真忘性相。是曰兼中到。
text_en: and without praise. Arrival within the Partial is inner trust. Following things, it is unobstructed; like a wooden boat, inwardly empty, empty and open, free and at ease. The Partial within the Real is compliance. Space is shattered into pieces, yet everywhere perfectly pervading; faculties and dusts are still. The Real within the Partial is delight. The moon in water and the image in a mirror originally have no arising or ceasing; how could there be tracks? Reaching within Integration is double clarity. The Real need not be empty; the Partial need not be solid. No turning away, no turning toward. It is also said: the workings of mind are extinguished, form and emptiness forgotten. There is no further concealment; the whole substance is manifest. This is called the Partial within the Real. Mountain is mountain, water is water. No one assigns names, no thing can be compared. This is called the Real within the Partial. Bare and naked, stark and clean, the face and features stand forth openly; filling heaven and filling earth, solely honored, without a second. This is called Coming within the Real. It is like the Son of Heaven within the realm, not borrowing the commands of Yu, Tang, Yao, or Shun. The eyes see and the ears hear, yet in the end borrow no other power. The ear does not enter into sound; sound does not block the ear-root. Inside, it has just turned the body, yet amid the dust it still bears no name. This is called Arrival within Integration. It is not mind, not object; not phenomena, not principle. From the beginning it is apart from names and appearances; innate suchness forgets nature and characteristics. This is called Reaching within Integration.

text_zh: 慈湛居士字禪海。丹州野野村人也。姓菅 原氏。假字清左衛門。原名廣次。少卜居京 師。嚮往鷹峯覺城和尚。執弟子禮。曩者請 予刊洞山語錄。既卒其業。今也刊曹山語 錄。附乎曩者所刊。以為壹帙。廣布法寶。所 鳩功利。以薦婦與女。又預修自冥福者乎。 婦也者慈照禪尼者。女也者智貞善女者。 將其芳名標出乎右。又記其事。而傳居士 勇為於不朽矣。
text_en: clan. His secular name was Seizaemon, and his original given name was Hirotsugu. In youth he made his home in the capital and admired Master Juecheng of Yingfeng, serving him with the rites of a disciple. Formerly he requested me to publish the Recorded Sayings of Dongshan. That work being completed, he now publishes the Recorded Sayings of Caoshan and appends it to what was formerly published, making a single volume, to spread the Dharma treasure widely. The merit and benefit thus gathered he dedicates to his wife and daughter, and also uses in advance to cultivate his own blessings in the unseen. The wife is the Chan nun Cizhao. The daughter is the virtuous woman Zhizhen. I set forth their honored names at the right, and also record this matter, thereby transmitting the layman's courageous deed into the undying.
